set.pl: Southwest point of Flynn Island ('Hermit Island', later 'Treasure Island'), Higgins Lake; island about 23 acres, now cottage lots
set.st: Israel 'Ezra' Porter Pritchard lived about twenty years as a hermit on Flynn Island ('Hermit Island', later 'Treasure Island') in Higgins Lake. He was found dead in his dugout in 1902 and buried in the potter's field of the Roscommon cemetery. The tale says he buried Civil War bounty-jumper money somewhere on the roughly 23-acre island; no amount is given and nothing was ever found. Israel Porter Pritchard, a former blacksmith and sailor, lived 20-odd years on the island as a county charge; a Bay City sailing party found him dead in his dug-out in Aug 1902. A 1970 Bay City Times feature by Roy L. Dodge, drawing on Lloyd Harman's 1929 account, says the island lies off Old Point Comfort and was first called Flynn's Island after the trapper Felix Flynn about 1870. About 1900, while Pritchard spent two winters with his son Houghton at Moorestown, boys burned his cabin; after that he lived in an old hunters' dugout on the island's southwest point, where he was found dead. The treasure rumours began only after his death.
pinev: Hunters' dugout on the SW point (Dodge 1970, after Harman 1929); his earlier cabin, elsewhere on the island, burned c.1900. SW tip read from the USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM island outline (tip ~44.4777,-84.7307); ring covers the SW lobe.

tw-mi-higgins-lake-flynn-island-hermit-c.t: No dig or find has ever been reported.
src: Bay City Times, 7 Jun 1970, p. 9, Roy L. Dodge, 'Treasure Isle Hermit / Higgins Lake Legend' (Newspapers.com 1184906703), after Lloyd Harman 1929 and Fred Hirzel of Moorestown
